missions.title: A Plank on the Same Bank
missions.stake: Idris needs to get a small dispatch to the east rack. He could take the regular route or ask Hesper to fit one light practice plank.
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can one short argument establish for all routes, and what changes when one link stops following its rule?

objectives.title: Build the bank strip and unfold both route branches with and without the plank.
Install one checked route and read the receipt at the east rack.

journal.text: The short bank strip ruled out every three-move route when each move switched banks. Tracing both branches found two three-move routes when we added the same-bank plank. The rack kept the rule used for the dispatch.

hints.text: Look for Idris’s bridge rail northeast of the market square.
Begin on Oak bank. The receiving rack is also on Oak bank. Fold one bank mark for each ordinary step.
Unfold the round-peg branch and the square-peg branch. See where three steps end when every link crosses.
Fit the one same-bank link on the practice rail. Unfold both branches again and see which new trails reach the rack.
Idris can use a light shortcut or keep the route people already share.
The proof tells which routes reach the rack. The weights named on the handover tell which loads can take each route.
Post the regular four-link route or fit the light-packet plank. Each leaves a different marked starting point on the east lane.
Use the plank passage or sign for the regular route at the turn post, then read the matching receipt by the east rack.
